small_guidance:
- The conv kernel uses BLOCK_S=256 with full OC_C=64 producing a 64×256 accumulator — try BLOCK_S=128 with num_warps=8 and add autotune configs (BLOCK_S ∈ {64,128,256}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}) since the current 64×256 tile likely spills registers and is the dominant cost.
- Tile OC as well (e.g. OC_C=32, BLOCK_S=128) so each program holds a smaller accumulator and more programs run in parallel; sweep (OC_TILE, BLOCK_S) pairs and key on (N, OC, H_out, W_out).
- Preload all weights once per program (small: 64·8·3·3 = 4608 floats) into registers/SRAM outside the spatial loop instead of re-issuing tl.load(w_ptr + w_off) inside the kh/kw/ic loops.
large_guidance:
- Recast the conv as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC_tile, spatial_tile) with BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=64–128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=IC·KH·KW=72 fully unrolled, using tl.dot for the matmul — this exploits tensor cores and is the standard high-performance layout.
- Fuse the bias add + GroupNorm + Tanh + HardSwish + residual + LogSumExp tail more aggressively: after computing x_conv tiles, write x_conv once, then have a single kernel that (a) computes per-group mean/invstd via two-pass over the channel block and (b) immediately consumes them to produce the LSE — currently this is split into two kernels touching x_conv twice.
- Consider a channels-last (NHWC) layout for x_conv so the LSE/GN reduction over channels is the contiguous axis, eliminating the 64-strided channel loop in fused_lse_kernel and enabling vectorized loads across C.
